question:
The length of a rectangular garden is decreasing at $2\ \text{m/min}$, while its width is increasing at $3\ \text{m/min}$. At an instant when its length is $30\ \text{m}$ and width is $20\ \text{m}$, determine:

(a) the rate of change of its area;

(b) the rate of change of its perimeter;

(c) the rate of change of the length of its diagonal.
explanation:
(a)
Let the length and width be $x$ and $y$, respectively. The given rates are
$$\frac{dx}{dt}=-2\ \text{m/min},\qquad \frac{dy}{dt}=3\ \text{m/min}$$
The area is $A=xy$. Therefore,
$$\frac{dA}{dt}=x\frac{dy}{dt}+y\frac{dx}{dt}$$
At $x=30$ and $y=20$,
$$\frac{dA}{dt}=30(3)+20(-2)=90-40=50\ \text{m}^2/\text{min}$$
Thus, the area is increasing at $50\ \text{m}^2/\text{min}$.

(b)
The perimeter is
$$P=2(x+y)$$
Differentiating with respect to time,
$$\frac{dP}{dt}=2\left(\frac{dx}{dt}+\frac{dy}{dt}\right)$$
$$\frac{dP}{dt}=2(-2+3)=2\ \text{m/min}$$
Thus, the perimeter is increasing at $2\ \text{m/min}$.

(c)
Let $d$ be the length of the diagonal. Then
$$d^2=x^2+y^2$$
At the given instant,
$$d=\sqrt{30^2+20^2}=10\sqrt{13}\ \text{m}$$
Differentiating $d^2=x^2+y^2$ with respect to time,
$$2d\frac{dd}{dt}=2x\frac{dx}{dt}+2y\frac{dy}{dt}$$
Therefore,
$$\frac{dd}{dt}=\frac{x\frac{dx}{dt}+y\frac{dy}{dt}}{d}$$
$$\frac{dd}{dt}=\frac{30(-2)+20(3)}{10\sqrt{13}}=0$$
Hence, the length of the diagonal is momentarily unchanged.

options.A:
(a) Area decreases at $50$ m$^2$/min
(b) Perimeter increases at $2$ m/min
(c) Diagonal decreases at $2$ m/min
options.B:
(a) Area increases at $40$ m$^2$/min
(b) Perimeter increases at $1$ m/min
(c) Diagonal is unchanged
options.C:
(a) Area increases at $90$ m$^2$/min
(b) Perimeter increases at $6$ m/min
(c) Diagonal increases at $1$ m/min
options.D:
(a) Area increases at $50$ m$^2$/min
(b) Perimeter increases at $2$ m/min
(c) Diagonal is momentarily unchanged
